standard_prerequisites.name: Pseudo-coherence is preserved by pulling back along the residue field map, so the fibre of the complex at the residue field is pseudo-coherent and its cohomology spaces are finite dimensional and vanish above some degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Establishes that the dimensions in the statement are finite and eventually zero, which is what the displayed complex uses.

standard_prerequisites.name: Every object of the derived category of a field is isomorphic to a complex with zero differentials, whose terms are the cohomology spaces
standard_prerequisites.use: Puts the fibre in the normal form to which the lifting statement applies.

standard_prerequisites.name: A map in the derived category between bounded complexes of projectives is represented by a map of complexes, and a map of finite free modules whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal is an isomorphism is an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the map of complexes in the uniqueness argument and upgrades its degreewise reductions to isomorphisms.

core_obligations: Observe that the fibre of the complex at the residue field is pseudo-coherent and that therefore its cohomology spaces are finite dimensional and vanish above some cutoff, which makes the integers of the statement well defined (proof lines 19565-19569).

Replace the fibre by a complex with zero differentials whose terms are the cohomology spaces, so that each term is a finite free module over the residue field of the prescribed dimension, and apply the lifting statement to obtain the existence of the displayed complex of free modules over the local ring (proof lines 19569-19573).

For the uniqueness, take two complexes of free modules with the same ranks representing the object and choose a map of complexes between them representing the isomorphism, which is possible because the representatives are bounded complexes of projectives (proof lines 19575-19582).

Observe that the induced map on the fibres is an isomorphism of complexes because the differentials on the fibres are zero, so the degreewise reductions of the map are isomorphisms of finite free modules; conclude that each degree of the map is an isomorphism, hence the two complexes are isomorphic and the uniqueness claim follows (proof lines 19583-19591).
proof_roadmap: Get finiteness and vanishing of the fibre cohomology from pullback of pseudo-coherence (proof lines 19565-19569).
Replace the fibre by a complex with zero differentials and invoke the lifting statement for existence (proof lines 19569-19573).
For uniqueness, represent the isomorphism by a map of complexes and upgrade its reductions modulo the maximal ideal to isomorphisms degreewise (proof lines 19575-19591).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that a pseudo-coherent object of the derived category of a local ring is represented by a complex of free modules whose ranks are the dimensions of the residue field fibres, and that this complex is unique up to isomorphism (statement lines 19547-19563). The proof splits into existence and uniqueness: existence follows by pulling pseudo-coherence to the residue field, replacing the fibre by a complex with zero differentials and applying the lifting statement, while uniqueness is proved by choosing a map of complexes between two representatives and observing that its reductions modulo the maximal ideal are isomorphisms because the induced map on the fibres is one, whence each degree is an isomorphism (proof lines 19565-19591). The degreewise reduction argument is the technical heart of the uniqueness half.
